issues.failure_explanation: The formula for $\hat{\bm{w}}(\Y)$ and the subsequent results require $\bm{K}(\Y)$ to be invertible. Assumption 2.1 and $\Y\in\mathcal{X}_{\neq}^{M}$ do not imply this; e.g., $\kappa(x,y)=1$ satisfies the assumption with $\bar{\kappa}=0$ but $\bm{K}$ is singular. Thus $\hat{\bm{w}}$ and $\bm{W}$ are not defined in general.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the assumption that $\bm{K}(\Y)$ is non-singular (e.g., for strictly positive definite kernels and distinct points) to Proposition 3.2, Theorem 3.3, and the MSIP construction.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 3.2 and its downstream uses in Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 are not valid for general kernels satisfying only Assumption 2.1.
issues.title: Missing invertibility assumption for K(Y) in steady-state and downstream results
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard local invertibility condition and preserves all main results for the kernels used in the paper.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: diagonal matrix $\bm{W}(\y)$ has entries corresponding to those of $\hw(\y)$ given by \eqref{eq:optimal_w}

issues.failure_explanation: The explicit map uses $\bm{W}(\Y)^{-1}$, where $\bm{W}$ is the diagonal matrix of optimal weights $\hat{w}_i(\Y)$. These weights can be zero, so $\bm{W}$ may be singular even when $\bm{K}$ and $\bm{\bar{K}}$ are non-singular. The map is then ill-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either assume $\bm{W}(\Y)$ is non-singular or define the iteration by solving the linear system $\bm{\bar{K}}(\Y)\bm{W}(\Y)\Y^{t+1}=\hvonem(\Y)$ instead of inverting $\bm{W}$.
issues.overall_effect: The MSIP fixed-point iteration is not well-defined in cases where some optimal weight vanishes.
issues.title: MSIP map requires invertibility of the weight matrix W
issues.why_classification: The repair is local (an extra assumption or a linear-system formulation) and does not change the main algorithmic idea.
